findings.title: DB125 legends: none under the nominal body, but pin-1 end legends sit 0.10-0.16 mm off it and five wire-side legends lie under their own wires
findings.evidence: DORABO DB125-3.5-XXP-C-S drawing T0-1 (maker PDF cached at .supervisor/r14_mechanics/db125.pdf, page 1): body depth 7.40, pin 3.90 from back and 3.50 to wire face, width Nx3.5, 0.42 mm side latch on the pin-1 side, general tolerance +/-0.30 (6-10) / +/-0.50 (10-30). Nominal body rectangles in PCB mm: J1 x3.9-11.3 y72.35-79.35; J400 y62.35-69.35; J121 y52.35-59.35; J410 x34.7-42.1 y8.5-22.5; J420 y24.5-38.5; J9 y40.5-54.5; J122 y62.75-80.25. Text boxes (pcbnew): no F.Silkscreen legend overlaps a nominal body (checked all 25). Nearest: 1:BAT+ 0.10 mm (J1, pin-1 north end, box y70.55-72.25), 4:RXI J410 0.10, 5:GND 0.10, 1:E1- 0.16 (J121), 1:S1 0.16 (J122). Pin-1 side: 0.42 latch plus 0.15 half-tolerance is 0.57 mm, and the repo VRML envelope (kilib/rocket.3dshapes/M3_DB125_*.wrl, 8.32x8.10x8.90 mm, centre -0.46) reaches 1.12 mm past nominal on pin 1, so it overlaps these boxes (glyph ~1 mm high, nominal glyph clearance ~0.45 mm to J1). Wire-side legends 1:SW (J400, x2.05-3.75), 1:4V8 (J410, x42.35-44.05), 4:RXI and 1:4V8 (J420), 4:TXO (J9) and 'SERVO + FROM HARNESS' (J122, x43.18-44.87, y62.4-81.75) lie 0.15-2.8 mm outside the wire face, centred on their own pin's wire exit line, so inserted wires cover about half of each. Pin 2/3 legends are on B.Silkscreen (by design, under the body, readable only from below / sled side). check_r10 K-legends tests nearest-connector only, not body or wire overlap.
findings.impact: No electrical effect. Once wired, the J1 BAT+ / E1- / S1 pin-1 end legends may be partly under the body latch and the wire-side legends are hidden by the wires they label, so polarity cannot be checked by eye after wiring; continuity check against the printed table is needed. Legends are not hidden under the terminal bodies at nominal.
findings.concrete_fix: Optional: move 1:BAT+, 1:E1-, 1:S1 (and 4:RXI on J410) 0.5 mm farther from the body (1:BAT+ has 1.0 mm free between the J400 and J1 envelopes: centre y70.4). State in ORDERING 8.3 that pin identity after wiring is by harness continuity check, not by silkscreen.

findings.title: C84 hand-fit: four bottom-side joints sit directly under its pads and R166 is 0.56 mm away
findings.evidence: C84 F(27.5,78.5) rot 90, pads 3.5x1.7 at (27.5,75.25) GND and (27.5,81.75) VLOGIC, courtyard 22.95-32.05 x 73.2-83.8. B.Cu pads with 0.0 mm XY gap to those pads: L1.2 (3V3), C7.2 (GND), C9.1 (3V3), C9.2 (GND); also L1.1 0.60, C7.1 0.90 mm. Top neighbour R166 courtyard gap 0.56 mm. Board is 1.6 mm. ORDERING 8.2 / R10_VALIDATION GAP-4 say only 'fit manually after both reflows using a separately validated local soldering process'; the supplier sheet has no manual profile.
findings.impact: Iron or hot-air heat on C84's pads is conducted through 1.6 mm FR4 and planes to the already-soldered L1, C7 and C9 joints; those can reflow, shift or tin-whisker; the polymer can's own limit is also unprofiled. Process risk, not a design failure.
findings.concrete_fix: Add to ORDERING 8.2: limit time and temperature, preheat from the top only with the bottom supported, re-inspect L1, C7, C9 after fitting and measure 3V3 and VLOGIC; or move C84 away from the bottom-side parts if the owner reopens placement.

rejected_or_closed_candidates: Wire-room margin 'only 0.053 mm' is conservative: the VRML envelope puts the wire face at 4.0 mm from the pin axis (west x3.4) against the maker's 3.5 nominal (3.8 at +0.3), so nominal-drawing room is about 5.80 (5.50 after the 0.3 sled tolerance).
